messages:
support-alex: FYI AcmeRetail just opened a ticket — dedicated pool dc-us-west-3 showing repeated throughput drops since 09:28 PDT. Customers see 5xx + p95/p99 latency spikes. I attached the error snippets and a short trace :grimacing:
maria: thx, can you paste their request profile and an example trace? service/tenant id?
support-alex: tenant=acme-retail-prod, sample request: short prompt then long continuation; attaching logs (snip) `503: queue timeout` and `ThrottleError: max_inflight`
jonathan: I pulled metrics — looks like the continuous-batcher window started oscillating around 09:27. Batcher window size metric shows rapid shrink/grow cycles. Link: https://grafana/redwood/d/abcd/queue-metrics :eyes:
kevin: hypothesis: the new queue-smoothing heuristic (enabled 2026-03-10) interacts poorly with max_batch_tokens when seq lengths vary a lot. Smoothing keeps window small, autoscaler sees low sustained QPS and refrains from scaling -> noisy-tenant microbursts starve others.
maria: can you repro locally with a mixed-length workload? if so we can test turning smoothing off for that pool.
jonathan: repro steps I used: run loadgen with mixed token lengths 16/128/512 at mean concurrency 120 across 10 clients. Script below:
```
# simplified repro
python tools/loadgen.py --hosts dc-us-west-3:443 --clients 10 --rps 400 --mix 0.5:16,0.3:128,0.2:512 --duration 600
```
I see oscillation in 30s cycles.
ashley: quick check on autoscaler logs: no scale-up events around 09:25-09:35. scale-decider returned false due to short duration spikes (<60s) per policy. config: `min_replicas=4, scale_threshold=60s, burst_window=30s`.
samir: could also be max_batch_tokens calc: if a few large sequences enter, batcher reduces effective batch size to honor token budget, but smoothing then tightens window and prefill drops. Combined effect -> throughput drop.
kevin: concrete mitigation: temporarily disable queue-smoothing flag for that dedicated pool or lower scale_threshold to 20s. Either will reduce time-to-scale or let batcher fill more aggressively. Which do we want as hotfix?
maria: prefer slower blast radius -> flip smoothing off for dc-us-west-3, monitor 15m. If good, we'll adjust autoscaler policy. Can someone prepare the flag toggle?
jonathan: prepping canary toggle now. @sre-bot starting rollout: `feature-toggle:queue_smoothing=false` pool=dc-us-west-3 canary=10%
sre-bot: rollouts/12345 started by jonathan — canary 10% -> 100% in 5m if no errors.
support-alex: I'll tell AcmeRetail we have a canary and will monitor, suggested workaround: reduce client concurrency.
kevin: also pushed a small safeguard: if max_batch_tokens calc would reduce batch size < min_batch (2), skip smoothing path. will open PR after hotfix.
ashley: after toggle: observed p95 down from 820ms -> 180ms in 8m window, throughput stable. autoscaler saw sustained queue increase and added 2 replicas at 09:44.
maria: nice. keep monitoring 30m, then we can plan config change (scale_threshold=30s, burst_window=45s) and a more robust token-aware smoothing.
samir: filed follow-up ticket INFR-7898 for scheduler tuning + regression test in the perf harness.
support-alex: passing update to customer: hotfix applied, monitoring, ticket linked to INFR-7898. Thanks team :tada:
maria: closing internal escalation once we confirm 1h stable. thx everyone.
